description: Fix the blank Annual Report PDF. ROOT CAUSE: in mgmt/backend/src/index.js the `convertDocxToPdfBulk` action handler forwards `req.base64` as the 5th argument to docx.dispatchBulkPdfConvert(...), but that 5th parameter is the placeholder `data` object and the frontend (mgmt/frontend/src/api.js convertDocxToPdfBulk) sends the placeholders under `req.data`, NOT `req.base64`. `req.base64` is undefined for this path, so dispatchBulkPdfConvert receives undefined, sends `data: {}` to the Render 'pdf_convert' job, and Render fills the report template with an EMPTY object. All docxtemplater loop sections ({#contributors}/{#expenses}/{#loans}/{#guarantors}) collapse to their inverted ({^...}) empty-state fallbacks and every scalar ({TOTAL_COLLECTION} etc.) resolves blank via nullGetter — producing the observed 3-page template-only PDF with no data. Receipts work because they use the batch path (convertDocxToPdfBatch -> req.items[].data). FIX: pass req.data (the placeholder set, including its nested arrays) instead of req.base64 in the convertDocxToPdfBulk handler. Add prove-first tests. Do NOT change PdfExport.jsx or api.js (frontend is confirmed correct); do NOT change the convertDocxToPdf single/consent handler (that path genuinely sends base64).
steps: In mgmt/backend/src/index.js, locate the `convertDocxToPdfBulk` handler (around line 1129-1138). It currently calls: docx.dispatchBulkPdfConvert(env, req.docType, req.year, req.recordId, req.base64, req.fileName, user, { force: !!req.force }). Change the 5th argument from req.base64 to req.data so the placeholder object (with nested arrays loans/guarantors/contributors/expenses) is forwarded to Render. Update the adjacent comment if it still implies base64 for this path.

Verify the change is scoped: the `convertDocxToPdf` handler just above (single/consent path, ~line 1122-1128) MUST keep using req.base64 — it genuinely sends a pre-filled .docx. Do not touch it. The batch handler already uses req.items and is correct.

Add a prove-first source-level contract test at mgmt/backend/test/pdf-export-bulk-data-wiring.test.mjs modeled on the existing frontend-payloads-pass-the-server-guard.test.mjs pattern (read source text, assert the two halves agree). It MUST assert: (a) the frontend api.js convertDocxToPdfBulk sends the placeholder set under the `data` key (parse mgmt/frontend/src/api.js and confirm the call body key is `data`, not `base64`); (b) the index.js convertDocxToPdfBulk handler forwards `req.data` (not `req.base64`) into docx.dispatchBulkPdfConvert as the argument that lands on dispatchBulkPdfConvert's `data` parameter. Write the assertion so it FAILS if the handler is reverted to req.base64. Include a self-check that the extractor actually found the handler (non-vacuous), following the 'the extractor is not vacuous' precedent in the model test.

Add a behavioral prove-first test that exercises dispatchBulkPdfConvert end-to-end through to the Render job body: in a test (e.g. add cases to a new mgmt/backend/test/pdf-export-report-data.test.mjs), stub env so RENDER_SERVICE_URL/RENDER_API_KEY are set and intercept the dispatched job payload (see how renderJobs.createAndDispatchJob is invoked and how existing render-* tests capture the outbound job / use fetch stubs — reuse that mechanism). Assert that when dispatchBulkPdfConvert is called with a report placeholder object containing NON-EMPTY contributors/expenses/loans/guarantors arrays (mirroring what PdfExport.jsx builds: contributors:[{SL_NO,NAME,VILLAGE,AMOUNT,...}], expenses:[...], loans:[...], guarantors:[...] plus scalars TOTAL_COLLECTION etc.), the outbound Render job payload's `data` preserves those arrays intact (same lengths, key names, nested field names) and is NOT flattened, dropped, or stringified. This is the assertion that would have caught the empty-data dispatch.

Add a Render-side prove-first test in mgmt/server-render (e.g. test/report-loops-fill.test.mjs) that feeds fillDocxTemplateFromBytes/fillDocxTemplateFromBase64 (mgmt/server-render/src/lib/docxRender.js) a minimal .docx template containing an {#contributors}{NAME}{/contributors} section (and optionally {^contributors}No contributors.) and asserts: given a non-empty contributors array the rendered docx text contains the row values and NOT the empty-state fallback; given an empty array it contains the fallback. If constructing a .docx fixture in-test is impractical, reuse any existing template/zip fixture helper already used by mgmt/server-render/test/docxRender.test.mjs. This locks the contract that Render renders loop rows when given arrays — proving the fix's data actually populates the report.
Run the full backend suite and confirm 1083 existing + new tests pass, 0 fail. Run the render suite and confirm green including the docxRender parity/drift test.
Prove the tests are meaningful: temporarily revert the index.js line to req.base64, confirm the wiring test AND the behavioral dispatch test FAIL, then restore the fix. Record this in findings.
acceptance_criteria: mgmt/backend/src/index.js convertDocxToPdfBulk handler passes req.data (not req.base64) as the 5th arg to docx.dispatchBulkPdfConvert.
The convertDocxToPdf (single/consent) handler is unchanged and still uses req.base64.
A source-level wiring test asserts the frontend sends `data` and the handler forwards req.data; it fails if reverted to req.base64.
A behavioral test asserts the Render job payload's `data` preserves non-empty contributors/expenses/loans/guarantors arrays intact when dispatchBulkPdfConvert is called with them.
A Render fill test asserts loop sections render rows for a non-empty array and the empty-state fallback for an empty array.
Backend suite: 1083 prior + new tests pass, 0 fail. Render suite: green (including the parity/drift test).
PdfExport.jsx and api.js data-building are unchanged.
verification: cd mgmt/backend && node --test --test-reporter=spec test/*.test.mjs (pass = 1083 + new, fail 0)
Revert-check: change req.data back to req.base64 in index.js, rerun the two new backend tests and confirm they FAIL, then restore req.data and confirm they PASS.
findings:
FIX: mgmt/backend/src/index.js convertDocxToPdfBulk handler now forwards req.data (not req.base64) as the 5th arg to docx.dispatchBulkPdfConvert (that param is `data`, the placeholder set with nested loans/guarantors/contributors/expenses arrays). The adjacent comment was updated to explain the server-side fill and why req.base64 (undefined here) produced the blank report. The convertDocxToPdf single/consent handler is UNCHANGED (still req.base64 — a real pre-filled .docx), and PdfExport.jsx + api.js were not touched.

TESTS ADDED (all prove-first):
1. mgmt/backend/test/pdf-export-bulk-data-wiring.test.mjs — source-level contract, modeled on frontend-payloads-pass-the-server-guard.test.mjs. Reads api.js (asserts the call body sends placeholders under `data`, never `base64`) and index.js (parses the dispatchBulkPdfConvert(...) arg list and asserts the 5th positional arg is exactly `req.data`, not `req.base64`), plus a check that the single/consent handler still sends req.base64. Includes a non-vacuous 'the extractor is not vacuous' block and a control that proves the positional assertion throws on a req.base64 shape.
2. mgmt/backend/test/pdf-export-report-data.test.mjs — behavioral: drives the real dispatchBulkPdfConvert with a PdfExport-shaped placeholder object (non-empty contributors/expenses/loans/guarantors + scalars), stubs globalThis.fetch to capture the outbound Render job body, and asserts payload.data deep-equals the input (arrays same length, nested field names/values preserved, not flattened/dropped/stringified). getDocxTemplate is satisfied without Drive by seeding a docx_templates row + the KV cache key docxtpl:<drive_file_id>:<updated_at>. A control asserts an empty placeholder set reaches Render as {} (the observed symptom).
3. mgmt/server-render/test/report-loops-fill.test.mjs — Render fill: builds a minimal .docx in-test with PizZip containing {#contributors}{NAME}{/contributors} + {^contributors}No contributors.{/contributors}, feeds it through fillDocxTemplateFromBase64/FromBytes, asserts a non-empty array renders one row per entry (no fallback) and an empty array / empty object {} renders the fallback.

VERIFICATION (Node v22.23.2, host-based; no Cloudflare/Render creds):
- Backend: node --test test/*.test.mjs -> tests 1086, pass 1086, fail 0 (baseline 1079 + 7 new).
- Render: node --test test/*.test.mjs -> tests 203, pass 203, fail 0 (baseline 199 + 4 new, incl. the docxRender parity/drift test).

REVERT-CHECK: temporarily reverted the handler to req.base64. The wiring test's 'the index.js handler forwards req.data' case FAILED (as designed), then restored req.data and all pass. NOTE: the behavioral dispatch test (#2) calls dispatchBulkPdfConvert DIRECTLY (below the handler), so it is intentionally revert-insensitive — its job per the acceptance criteria is to prove the dispatch layer preserves non-empty arrays intact, while the source-level wiring test (#1) is the guard that fails on the handler revert. Together they cover both the wiring and the data-preservation contract.
